description: The plot titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-2” illustrates how a sparsity ratio (proportion of SDPA output values below a 1e-2 threshold) varies across model layers for three different measurement conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Layer” on a linear scale, spanning from 0 to 23 with major tick labels at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio” on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with regularly spaced tick labels every 0.2. Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line with no markers (“sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03”) that starts near 0.18 at layer 0, drops to roughly 0.03 by around layer 2, stays near 0.03–0.04 through roughly layers 3–8, and then gradually declines toward about 0.01 by around layers 19–21 and near 0.00 by layer 23; an orange dotted line with no markers (“sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44”) that begins near 1.00 at layer 0, decreases to about 0.75 by around layer 4 and about 0.45–0.50 by around layers 8–9, continues downward to roughly 0.18–0.22 around layers 13–17, and then shows oscillations and partial increases late in the network, including around 0.28 at about layer 19, about 0.39 near layer 21, about 0.24 near layer 22, and ending near 0.38 at layer 23; and a green dash-dot line with no markers (“sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33”) that starts near 1.00 at layer 0, declines to about 0.65–0.70 by around layer 4 and about 0.35 by around layer 7, then continues down to about 0.16–0.18 around layers 10–11 and about 0.10 around layers 15–18, shows a small bump to roughly 0.12 near layer 21, and ends near 0.05 by layer 23.
